dedupe_keys.name: silvis lab wildland urban interface change maps for the us 1990 to 2020

description: The SILVIS wildland-urban interface (WUI) change dataset maps where housing meets or mingles with wildland vegetation across the conterminous United States for 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2020, separating intermix WUI, where houses sit among vegetation, from interface WUI, where houses border large vegetated areas. Version 4, updated in February 2025, is produced by the SILVIS Lab at the University of Wisconsin–Madison and described by Radeloff and others (2023) in Science. The maps are available free from the SILVIS website as shapefiles by state and as a file geodatabase, with state and county summary totals in Excel and a web map; no licence is named on the page read. Caveats: WUI classes are derived from census housing density and land cover, so they mark potential exposure, not fire hazard itself, and census block boundaries limit spatial detail. It supports wildfire exposure analysis of housing, power lines, roads and other infrastructure at the wildland edge and trend studies of growth into fire-prone areas; a related record is the USFS Wildfire Hazard Potential map.
